title: Build: Remove superfluous automoc commands
description:
Setting CMAKE_AUTOMOC to ON causes all targets to be checked
for MOC\UIC\RCC requirements and isn't required.

The settings on the wireshark target aren't required either.

notes.body:
Given the little I know about Qt, I may be barking up the wrong tree here, but CMake seemed to be running a batch file checking for AutoMOC requirements on every target.

After the removals in this MR, Wireshark (RelwithDebInfo) builds OK for me without the superfluous calls in the build, we'll see what the pipelines make of it.

Which version of CMake are you using? Setting CMAKE_AUTOMOC to ON (removed in !3008) runs `moc` on all targets, which is why I tried to limit it to buggy versions of CMake (3.20.0 to 3.20.2).

As far as I can tell, setting the AUTOMOC property on the wireshark target is necessary for MSBuild and other multi-config generators, otherwise you run into the issue described in https://ask.wireshark.org/question/22651/i-have-fatal-error-lnk1181-when-rebuild-wireshark-on-window/. A fresh build fails for me here on Windows if AUTOMOC isn't set for the wireshark target. Doing so shouldn't result in `moc` running on all targets.

I'm using the version that comes with VS 16.9.4 which is 3.19.20122902-MSVC_2.

The pipelines with this change all seem to have succeeded (the Windows one is very noisy with build timings, they can probably be dispensed with).  I find the GitLab pipeline output almost useless when looking at things such as this so I'm not entirely certain.
I forgot to mention that I made my local test builds from a clean build dir.

I built the current master using different versions of CMake on macOS and Windows and checked for "Automatic ..." messages in the build output.
"wireshark AUTO*" below indicates that the AUTOMOC, AUTOUIC, and AUTORCC properties were set on the "wireshark" target.
CMAKE_AUTO* indicates that the CMAKE_AUTOMOC, CMAKE_AUTOUIC, and CMAKE_AUTORCC variables were set to ON in the top-level CMakeFile.

It looks like CMake 3.20.0 and later need the AUTOMOC, AUTOUIC, and AUTORCC properties set on the "wireshark" target, either explictly or implicitly via the CMAKE_AUTOMOC, CMAKE_AUTOUIC, and CMAKE_AUTORCC variables. The former adds "Automatic MOC and UIC" for "wireshark" while the latter adds them for what appears to be all of our targets. I think it sense to set the AUTOMOC, AUTOUIC, and AUTORCC properties for "wireshark". We could do so only for CMake 3.20.0 and later if we're concerned about the extra AUTOMOC and AUTOUIC run.
I wonder if that's another regression in CMake 3.20 that's causing us to require the addition to the wireshark target?

I think that's the key question. The behavior matches the description in [CMake issue 22085](https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/22085), but the nightly build I tested (3.20.20210515-g5026ee2) still fails in our case.
Maybe need to follow up on that CMake issue that it's still present for us.  Maybe because the qtui lib target is added by a different CMakeLists.txt from the Wireshark target?

changes_data.diff:
@@ -1151,13 +1151,6 @@ ws_find_package(Systemd BUILD_sdjournal HAVE_SYSTEMD)
 
 # Build the Qt GUI?
 if(BUILD_wireshark)
-	if(CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_GREATER "3.19.999" AND CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_LESS "3.20.2")
-		# https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/cmake/-/issues/22085
-		set(CMAKE_AUTOMOC ON)
-		set(CMAKE_AUTOUIC ON)
-		set(CMAKE_AUTORCC ON)
-	endif()
-
 	# Untested, may not work if CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH gets overwritten
 	# somewhere. The if WIN32 in this place is annoying as well.
 	if(WIN32)
@@ -2459,9 +2452,6 @@ if(BUILD_wireshark AND QT_FOUND)
 		LINK_FLAGS "${WS_LINK_FLAGS}"
 		FOLDER "Executables"
 		INSTALL_RPATH "${EXECUTABLE_INSTALL_RPATH}"
-		AUTOMOC ON
-		AUTOUIC ON
-		AUTORCC ON
 	)
 	if(MSVC)
 		set_target_properties(wireshark PROPERTIES LINK_FLAGS_DEBUG "${WS_MSVC_DEBUG_LINK_FLAGS}")
